title: Calculate the Count of Connected Components in LCM Graph

content.problemStatement:
You receive an array of integers `nums` of size `n` and a **positive** integer `threshold`.

There is a graph consisting of `n` nodes with the `ith` node having a value of `nums[i]`. Two nodes `i` and `j` in the graph are connected via an **undirected** edge if `lcm(nums[i], nums[j]) <= threshold`.

Output the number of **connected components** in this graph.

A **connected component** is a subgraph of a graph in which there exists a path between any two vertices, and no vertex of the subgraph shares an edge with a vertex outside of the subgraph.

The term `lcm(a, b)` denotes the **least common multiple** of `a` and `b`.

**Example 1:**

**Input:** nums = [2,4,8,3,9], threshold = 5

**Output:** 4

**Explanation:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2024/10/31/example0.png)

The four connected components are `(2, 4)`, `(3)`, `(8)`, `(9)`.

**Example 2:**

**Input:** nums = [2,4,8,3,9,12], threshold = 10

**Output:** 2

**Explanation:**

![](https://assets.leetcode.com/uploads/2024/10/31/example1.png)

The two connected components are `(2, 3, 4, 8, 9)`, and `(12)`.

**Constraints:**

* `1 <= nums.length <= 105`
* `1 <= nums[i] <= 109`
* All elements of `nums` are unique.
* `1 <= threshold <= 2 * 105`
